smells.finding: render_human() grows to ~50 lines with this diff (added a 2-line constraints block and a 3-line anchors block), consistent with the file's existing adapter-function scale (state()/render_human() are the single StateView builder/formatter and already handled several fields before this change); not egregious.
no classes touched; the module is function-based.

render_human() (scripts/checklist_engine.py ~1670-1689) already generalizes the pre/postconditions rendering into one loop over [(which, open_conds), ...] specifically to avoid repeating the 'if populated: append label; extend indented lines' shape (see the file's own inline note: '(rework 1, non-blocking Fowler note) share the label+lines shape with _next_verbs()'s sections pattern instead of repeating it per list'). The new constraints block and the new anchors block each re-introduce that exact shape as two more separate if-statements immediately below the already-generalized loop, rather than folding constraints/anchors into the same iteration (e.g. [('preconditions', ...), ('postconditions', ...), ('constraints', active.get('constraints') or []), ('anchors', anchor_lines)]). Minor and non-blocking -- 5 lines total, correctness is unaffected -- but it is the same pattern the prior rework's own comment flagged and did not fully close out. Worth folding in on the next touch to this function.

the two new helpers (_anchor_category_items, _render_anchor_lines) and the new state()/render_human() reads operate purely on their own parameters (items/anchors/active dict); no reaching into a sibling object's internals.
no repeated group of parameters/fields traveling together was introduced; anchors and constraints are independent optional Task fields, each handled on its own.

isinstance dispatch over str/list/dict shapes in _anchor_category_items/_render_anchor_lines looks primitive-obsession-adjacent, but this is loosely-typed external JSON corpus data (Task.anchors is not a project-owned domain type) with 3 shapes independently confirmed present in the live corpus (20+ archived execute.json files plus the shipped EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json) -- the same shape-dispatch idiom the rest of the file already uses for condition/evidence/status_detail parsing. Not a case of a primitive standing in for a missing domain concept.
both new helpers take exactly one parameter each.

one coherent conceptual fix (RAIL dedup + anchors/constraints projection) touches 3 functions in ONE file (_rail, state, render_human) plus 2 new co-located helpers -- concentrated, not scattered across unrelated modules.

state()/render_human() are the general-purpose StateView projection/formatter and already change whenever a new Task field needs surfacing to the agent; adding anchors/constraints is the same axis of change as every other field already there (imperative, preconditions, postconditions, next_verbs), not a new, unrelated reason for these functions to change.
no chained attribute/call access introduced; the new code reads dict.get() one level deep.

the opposite is true here -- _render_anchor_lines explicitly documents that it handles only the 3 shapes CONFIRMED present in the live corpus and renders nothing for an unrecognized 4th shape 'rather than guessing at a format the corpus doesn't actually use' -- grounded in verified evidence, not built out for a hypothetical future need.

the new docstrings/comments cite issue #420, the specific corpus evidence (line/file references), and a concrete failure mode already caught in rework (the character-explosion bug) -- they explain WHY a non-obvious shape-handling choice was made, matching the file's pre-existing dense-comment convention throughout (CLAUDE.md/global-everyone.md: 'agent-facing, dense by design'); they are not covering for unclear code -- the code itself (isinstance branches, early returns) reads plainly on its own.
